name: Catholic Cross References — our own references
stage: Stage 3 begun: Genesis — the first book beyond the deuterocanon. (Stage 2, the deuterocanon complete: Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, Tobias, Judith, Baruch, 1–2 Machabees, and the additions to Esther and Daniel.)
license: Public domain (Unlicense). The passages quoted as evidence are the original Douay-Rheims Bible (1582–1610), also public domain.
about: References built by this project on top of the seed (cross-references.json), book by book. The deuterocanon is complete: Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, Tobias, Judith, Baruch (with the Epistle of Jeremias), 1 and 2 Machabees, and the added chapters of Esther and Daniel — each in both directions, the book pointing to the rest of Scripture and the rest of Scripture pointing to it. Every reference was checked against both passages: the short quotations under "evidence" are the very words on which the link rests, taken from the original Douay-Rheims text. Kinds: quotation (one passage takes up the other's words), allusion (an echo a reader is meant to catch), parallel (the same event, person, or account in both), theme (the same doctrine or image developed in both). Nothing here is copied from any modern copyrighted apparatus; pairs the seed already carries are not repeated.

evidence.target: there be a bell of gold and a pomegranate

45:10.note: Aaron’s ringing hem in Sirach is the bell of gold and pomegranate of Exodus.

evidence.source: for a memorial, according to the number of the tribes of Israel
evidence.target: thou shalt grave them with the names of the children of Israel

45:13.note: The stones graven for a memorial by the tribes’ number are the shoulder stones of Exodus, graven with the names of Israel’s children.

evidence.source: A crown of gold upon his mitre graven with a seal of holiness
evidence.target: a plate of the purest gold: wherein thou shalt grave

45:14.note: The gold crown on Aaron’s mitre, graven as a seal of holiness, is the plate of purest gold of Exodus, graven Holy to the Lord.

evidence.source: Moyses filled his hands, & anointed him with holy oil
evidence.target: pouring upon Aaron's head, he anointed, & consecrated him

45:18.note: Moses anointing Aaron with holy oil is the consecration of Leviticus 8.

evidence.source: He did prodigious things unto them, and consumed them in flame of fire
evidence.target: fire also coming forth from our Lord, slew the two hundred fifty men

45:24.note: The flame that consumed Dathan’s company in Sirach is the fire from the Lord that slew the two hundred fifty men.

evidence.source: Priesthood should be to him and to his seed for ever
evidence.target: to him as to his seed the covenant of priesthood for ever

45:30.note: The covenant of peace made with Phinees is the covenant of everlasting priesthood of Numbers 25.

evidence.source: the great and holy God heard him in hail-stones of exceeding great force
evidence.target: our Lord sent upon them great stones from heaven

46:6.note: The hail-stones that answered Jesus Nave’s prayer are the great stones from heaven at Beth-horon.

evidence.source: delivered out of danger from among the number of six hundred thousand
evidence.target: to him I will give the Land, that he hath trodden

46:10.note: Of the six hundred thousand, Caleb alone with Josue was delivered to enter; Deuteronomy gives Caleb the land he trod.

evidence.source: in the oblation of an immaculate lamb
evidence.target: Samuel took one sucking lamb, and offered it a whole holocaust

46:19.note: Samuel’s oblation of the lamb before the thunder is the sucking lamb offered at Masphath.

evidence.source: he notified to the king, and shewed him the end of his life
evidence.target: why hast thou disquieted me, that I should be raised up?

46:23.note: Samuel notifying the king after his sleep is Samuel raised for Saul at Endor.

evidence.source: with a stone of the sling he overthrew the boasting of Goliath
evidence.target: took one stone, and cast it with the sling

47:5.note: David overthrowing Goliath’s boasting with the sling-stone is the stone taken from the scrip in 1 Kings.

evidence.source: rooted out the Philisthiims the adversaries even until this present day
evidence.target: David struck the Philisthiims, and humbled them

47:8.note: David rooting out the Philistine adversaries is the victory the Chronicles record at Geth.

evidence.source: gave him a testament of the kingdom, and the seat of glory
evidence.target: thy house shall be faithful, and thy Kingdom for ever

47:13.note: The testament of the kingdom given to David is Nathan’s promise: thy kingdom for ever, thy throne firm continually.

evidence.source: thou didst multiply dark sayings in comparisons
evidence.target: spake three thousand parables: and his songs were a thousand & five

47:17.note: Salomon’s multiplied comparisons are the three thousand parables and thousand and five songs of 3 Kings.

evidence.source: Thou didst gather gold as copper, and filledst silver as lead
evidence.target: made so great plenty of silver in Jerusalem as it were of stones

47:20.note: Salomon filling silver as lead is the silver made as plenty as stones in Jerusalem.

evidence.source: to make the Kingdom divided
evidence.target: Behold I will rent the Kingdom out of the hand of Salomon

47:23.note: The kingdom made divided after Salomon is Ahias’s sentence: I will rent the kingdom out of his hand.

evidence.source: he brought down fire from heaven thrice
evidence.target: the fire of our Lord fell, and devoured the holocaust

48:3.note: Elias bringing down fire from heaven is first the fire that fell on Carmel and devoured the holocaust.

evidence.source: Who didst raise up the dead from hell, from the lot of death
evidence.target: the soul of the child returned into him, and he revived

48:5.note: Elias raising the dead is the widow’s son, whose soul returned into him and he revived.

evidence.source: Who hearest judgement in Sina, and in Horeb judgements of defence
evidence.target: stand in the mount before our Lord: and behold our Lord passeth

48:7.note: Elias hearing judgment in Horeb is Elias standing in the mount as the Lord passed by.

evidence.source: makest Prophets successors after thee
evidence.target: Eliseus the son of Saphat, which is of Abelmeula

48:8.note: The prophet made successor after Elias is Eliseus the son of Saphat, anointed at God’s word in Horeb.

evidence.source: his spirit was complete in Eliseus
evidence.target: The spirit of Elias hath rested upon Eliseus

48:13.note: Elias’s spirit completed in Eliseus is the spirit the sons of the prophets saw resting on him at Jericho.

evidence.source: his body prophesied being dead
evidence.target: when it had touched the bones of Eliseus, the man revived

48:14.note: Eliseus’ body prophesying dead is the corpse that revived on touching his bones.

evidence.source: brought in water into the midst thereof, and digged a rock with iron
evidence.target: stopped the upper fountain of the waters of Gihon

48:19.note: Ezechias bringing water into the city is his stopping of Gihon’s upper fountain and turning it underneath.

evidence.source: spreading their hands, they lifted them up to heaven
evidence.target: Lord God of Israel, which sittest upon the cherubins

48:22.note: The people lifting their hands to heaven is Ezechias spreading Rabsaces’ letter and praying before the Lord of the cherubins.

evidence.source: comforted the mourners in Sion
evidence.target: Be comforted, be comforted my people, saith your God

48:27.note: Isaias comforting the mourners in Sion is the voice that opens his fortieth chapter: Be comforted, my people.

evidence.source: to reconcile the heart of the father to the son
evidence.target: he shall convert the heart of the fathers to the children

48:10.note: Sirach’s charge laid on the returning Elias is Malachias’s prophecy, nearly in its own words.

evidence.source: to restore the tribes of Jacob
evidence.target: thou shouldst be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob

48:10.note: The second half of Elias’s charge is Isaias’s word to the servant: to raise up the tribes of Jacob.

evidence.source: to reconcile the heart of the father to the son
evidence.target: he may convert the hearts of the fathers unto the children

48:10.note: The angel announces John in Elias’s spirit with Sirach’s own charge: to convert the hearts of the fathers unto the children.

evidence.source: he took away the abominations of impiety
evidence.target: Josias took away: that he might establish the words of the law

49:3.note: Josias taking away the abominations is his purging of Juda and Jerusalem in 4 Kings 23.

evidence.source: They burnt the chosen city of holiness, & made the ways thereof desolate
evidence.target: the house of the common people the Chaldees burnt with fire

49:8.note: The city burnt in Jeremie’s hand is the burning Jeremias himself records: the Chaldees burnt the houses with fire.

evidence.source: which he shewed him in the chariot of Cherubs
evidence.target: in the firmament, that was over the head of the Cherubs

49:10.note: Ezechiel’s sight of glory in the chariot of cherubs is the throne seen above the cherubs’ heads by the river Chobar.

evidence.source: Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their days built the house
evidence.target: set on the head of Jesus the son of Josedec the grand Priest

49:14.note: Jesus the son of Josedec, builder of the house with Zorobabel, is the high priest crowned in Zacharias.

evidence.source: who erected us our walls overthrown, and set up the gates and locks
evidence.target: the wall was finished the five and twentieth day

49:15.note: Nehemias erecting the overthrown walls is the wall finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul.

evidence.source: his bones were visited, and after death they prophesied
evidence.target: God shall visit you, carry out my bones from hence with you

49:18.note: Joseph’s bones visited after death are the bones Moses carried out of Egypt, as Joseph had adjured Israel.

evidence.source: submit your neck to the yoke, and let your soul receive discipline
evidence.target: Take up my yoke upon you, and learn of me

51:34.note: Wisdom’s invitation to bow the neck under her yoke is taken up on Christ’s lips: Take up my yoke upon you, and learn of me.

evidence.source: I have laboured a little, and have found much rest to myself
evidence.target: all that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you

51:35.note: The rest Sirach found after a little labour is the refreshment Christ promises to all that labour and are burdened.

evidence.source: Forgive thy neighbour hurting thee: & then shall thy sins be loosed
evidence.target: if you will forgive men their offences, your heavenly father will forgive you

28:2.note: Sirach’s rule of forgiveness is the Lord’s own exposition of the prayer: forgive, and your Father will forgive you.

evidence.source: then shall thy sins be loosed to thee when thou prayest
evidence.target: when you shall stand to pray, forgive if you have ought

28:2.note: Forgiveness at prayer, in Sirach tied to the hour of praying, is Christ’s rule for standing to pray.

evidence.source: Say not: He hath made me err
evidence.target: when he is tempted, say that he is tempted of God

15:12.note: Sirach forbids the excuse James forbids: let no man say he is tempted of God.

evidence.source: Son, coveting wisdom, keep justice, & God will give her to thee
evidence.target: let him ask of God who giveth to all men aboundantly

1:33.note: The wisdom God gives the son who covets and keeps justice is the wisdom James bids the lacking ask of the God who gives abundantly.

evidence.source: come not to him with a double heart
evidence.target: Aman double of mind is inconstant in all his ways

1:36.note: Sirach’s double heart, barred from coming to God, is James’s double-minded man, inconstant in all his ways.

evidence.source: Be mild to hear the word, thou mayst understand
evidence.target: be swift to hear, but slow to speak, and slow to anger

5:13.note: Sirach’s mildness to hear the word is James’s rule in brief: swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.

evidence.source: If thou blow upon a spark, it will burn as a fire
evidence.target: Behold how much fire what a great wood it kindleth?

28:14.note: The spark blown into flame in Sirach is James’s little fire kindling a great wood — both are the tongue.

evidence.source: not so as they that have perished by their tongue
evidence.target: the tongue, is fire, a whole world of iniquity

28:22.note: More have perished by the tongue than by the sword, says Sirach; James names that tongue a fire, a whole world of iniquity.

evidence.source: gold and silver are tried in the fire, but acceptable men in the furnace
evidence.target: much more precious than gold (which is proved by the fire)

2:5.note: Acceptable men tried in the furnace as gold in the fire is Peter’s probation of faith, more precious than gold proved by fire.

evidence.source: Say not: I have sinned, and what sorrowful thing hath chanced to me?
evidence.target: not knowing that the benignity of God bringeth thee to penance?

5:4.note: The sinner who presumes on God’s patience in Sirach is the man Paul warns: that patience is meant to bring him to penance.

evidence.source: I have found me rest, and now I will eat of my goods alone
evidence.target: thou hast much goods laid up for many years, take thy rest, eat

11:19.note: The rich man’s soliloquy in Sirach — I have found rest, now I will eat of my goods — is spoken again by the fool in the parable.

evidence.source: he must leave all to others, and shall die
evidence.target: the things that thou hast provided, whose shall they be?

11:20.note: Sirach’s rich man, who must leave all to others and die, meets God’s question in the parable: whose shall those things be?

evidence.source: the first begotten before all creatures
evidence.target: the first-born of all creature

24:5.note: Wisdom’s self-praise as first-begotten before all creatures is the title Paul gives Christ, the first-born of all creature.

evidence.source: Inhabit in Jacob, and inherit in Israel, and take root in mine elect
evidence.target: The Word Was Made Flesh, and dwelt in us

24:13.note: Wisdom is commanded to take her dwelling in Jacob; the Word himself is made flesh and dwells among us.

evidence.source: Inhabit in Jacob, and inherit in Israel
evidence.target: delivered it to Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved

24:13.note: Baruch’s wisdom, found out by God and delivered to Jacob and Israel, is Sirach’s wisdom commanded to inhabit in Jacob.

evidence.source: shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst
evidence.target: he that cometh to me, shall not hunger

24:29.note: Christ answers wisdom’s banquet and reverses it: they that eat her hunger still; he that cometh to him shall not hunger, and shall never thirst.

evidence.source: Put thy treasure in the precepts of the Highest
evidence.target: heap up to yourselves treasures in heaven

29:14.note: Treasure laid up in the precepts of the Highest is treasure heaped up in heaven, where neither rust nor moth corrupts.

evidence.source: but pray our Lord, and he will cure thee
evidence.target: the prayer of faith shall save the sick

38:9.note: In sickness Sirach bids the son pray to the Lord who will cure him; James promises the prayer of faith shall save the sick.

evidence.source: Before man there is life and death, good and evil
evidence.target: set before thee this day life and good, and contrarywise death and evil

15:18.note: Life and death, good and evil set before man is Moses’ sentence in Deuteronomy, which Sirach takes up.

evidence.source: to which thou wilt, stretch forth thine hand
evidence.target: I have proposed to you life and death, blessing and cursing

15:17.note: The hand stretched forth to fire or water answers Moses’ proposal of life and death, blessing and cursing, with its command to choose life.

evidence.source: after his own image he made him
evidence.target: God created man to his own image

17:1.note: Man made after God’s own image is Genesis’ first word on his creation.

evidence.source: God created man of the earth
evidence.target: Our Lord God therefore formed man of the slime of the earth

17:1.note: Man created of the earth is man formed of the slime of the earth.

evidence.source: he had dominion of beasts and fowls
evidence.target: rule over the fishes and the sea, and fowls of the air

17:4.note: The dominion God put over beasts and fowls is the blessing of Genesis: rule over the fishes of the sea and the fowls of the air.

evidence.source: He created of him an helper like to himself
evidence.target: let us make him a help like unto himself

17:5.note: The helper like to himself, created of the man, is the help like unto himself that God makes in Genesis.

evidence.source: From the beginning and before the worlds was I created
evidence.target: From eternity I was ordained & of old before the earth was made

24:14.note: Wisdom created before the worlds in Sirach is wisdom ordained from eternity, of old before the earth was made, in Proverbs.

evidence.source: All these things are the book of life, and the testament of the Highest
evidence.target: This is the book of the commandments of God

24:32.note: Sirach ends wisdom’s praise by naming her the book of life; Baruch names the same wisdom the book of the commandments of God.

evidence.source: As potter's clay is in his hand, to fashion and dispose it
evidence.target: as clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand

33:13.note: Man as potter’s clay in the Maker’s hand is Jeremias’s word in the potter’s house.

evidence.source: As potter's clay is in his hand, to fashion and dispose it
evidence.target: of the same clay maketh the vessels that are clean to use

33:13.note: The two deuterocanon books share the potter: Wisdom’s potter makes vessels clean and contrary of the same clay, as Sirach’s clay is fashioned at his pleasure.

evidence.source: Our Lord will not accept person against the poor
evidence.target: that accepteth not person nor gifts

35:16.note: The Lord who accepts no person against the poor is Moses’ God of gods, that accepteth not person nor gifts.

evidence.source: He will not despise the prayers of the pupil: nor the widow
evidence.target: He doth judgment to the pupil and the widow

35:17.note: The pupil and widow whose prayers God will not despise are the pupil and widow to whom he does judgment in Deuteronomy.

evidence.source: Raise up fury, and pour out wrath
evidence.target: Pour out thy wrath upon the Gentiles, that have not known thee

36:8.note: Sirach’s prayer for Israel takes up the psalm’s: Pour out thy wrath upon the Gentiles that have not known thee.

evidence.source: It is not to be said: This is worse than that
evidence.target: every creature of God is good, and nothing to be rejected

39:40.note: Sirach forbids saying of any work of God, this is worse than that; Paul forbids rejecting any creature of God received with thanksgiving.

evidence.source: an heavy yoke upon the children of Adam
evidence.target: with much toiling shalt thou eat thereof all the days of thy life

40:1.note: The heavy yoke on Adam’s children is the curse on the ground: with much toiling shalt thou eat thereof all thy life.

evidence.source: All things that are of the earth, shall return into the earth
evidence.target: because dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return

41:13.note: All things of the earth returning into the earth is Adam’s sentence: dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.

evidence.source: full of the glory of our Lord is his work
evidence.target: The heavens shew forth the glory of God

42:16.note: Sirach’s hymn opens where the psalm opens: the heavens shew forth the glory of God, and his work is full of it.

evidence.source: By the moon is the sign of a festival day
evidence.target: He made the moon for seasons

43:7.note: The moon that in Sirach signs the festival day is the moon God made for seasons in the psalm.

evidence.source: See the bow, and bless him that made it
evidence.target: my bow will I set in the clouds

43:12.note: The bow Sirach bids us see and bless its Maker for is the bow God set in the clouds as the sign of the covenant.

evidence.source: Therefore are the treasures opened, & the clouds fly forth as birds
evidence.target: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow

43:15.note: The treasures opened in Sirach, out of which snow and hail fly at God’s command, are Job’s treasures of the snow.

evidence.source: Water quencheth burning fire, and alms resisteth sins
evidence.target: alms delivereth from death, and that is it which purgeth sins

3:33.note: Alms resisting sins in Sirach is Tobias’s angel’s word: alms delivereth from death and purgeth sins.

evidence.source: he was captive in the days of Salmanasar the king of the Assyrians
evidence.target: the king of Assyrians took Samaria, and transferred Israel unto the Assyrians

1:2.note: Tobias's captivity under Salmanasar is the carrying away of Israel into Assyria told at the end of 4 Kings.

evidence.source: the golden calves, which Jeroboam the king of Israel had made
evidence.target: he made two golden calves, and said to them

1:5.note: The calves Tobias alone refused to worship are the two Jeroboam made and set up for Israel.

evidence.source: the hungry he nourished
evidence.target: I was an hungered, and you gave me to eat

1:20.note: Tobias nourishing the hungry stands behind the King's word: I was an hungered, and you gave me to eat.

evidence.source: to the naked he gave cloths
evidence.target: naked, and you covered me

1:20.note: Clothing the naked is counted by the King as done to himself: naked, and you covered me.

evidence.source: be given to posterity of his patience, as also of holy Job
evidence.target: Our Lord gave, and our Lord hath taken away

2:12.note: The book itself sets Tobias beside holy Job: his blindness is permitted that posterity may have an example of patience like Job's.

evidence.source: our Lord permitted to chance unto him, that an example might be given
evidence.target: but that the works of God may be manifested in him

2:12.note: Both blindnesses are permitted not for the sufferer's sin but for what God will shew in them: an example of patience in Tobias, the works of God in the man born blind.

evidence.source: his life, if it be in probation, shall be crowned
evidence.target: when he hath been proved, he shall receive the crown of life

3:21.note: Sara's certainty — the life in probation shall be crowned — is James's crown of life for the man who has been proved.

evidence.source: turn not away thy face from any poor person
evidence.target: turn not away thy face from the needy

4:7.note: Tobias charges his son in Sirach's very words: turn not away thy face from the poor.

evidence.source: thou doest treasure up to thyself a good reward in the day of necessity
evidence.target: heap up to yourselves treasures in heaven

4:10.note: Alms treasured up as a good reward against the day of necessity is Christ's treasure heaped up in heaven.

evidence.source: thou doest treasure up to thyself a good reward
evidence.target: Put thy treasure in the precepts of the Highest, & it shall profit thee

4:10.note: Sirach's treasure put in the Highest's precepts, profiting more than gold, is the good reward Tobias bids his son treasure up by alms.

evidence.source: let not the hire of thy hired servant remain with thee at all
evidence.target: The work of thy hireling shall not abide with thee until morning

4:15.note: Tobias's wage rule is the law's own word: the hireling's hire shall not abide with thee until morning.

evidence.source: Whosoever hath wrought any thing for thee, pay him his hire immediately
evidence.target: the same day thou shalt pay him the price of his labour

4:15.note: Pay him the same day, says Deuteronomy; pay him his hire immediately, says Tobias — one precept in two voices.

evidence.source: pay him his hire immediately
evidence.target: which is defrauded of you, cryeth: and their cry hath entered into the ears

4:15.note: The hire Tobias commands to be paid at once is the very hire James hears crying to the Lord of Sabboth when it is kept back.

evidence.source: That which thou hatest to be done to thee by another
evidence.target: whatsoever you will that men do to you, do you also to them

4:16.note: Tobias gives the rule in its negative form — do not to another what thou hatest done to thee; Christ states it positively and calls it the Law and the Prophets.

evidence.source: Eat thy bread with the hungry & needy
evidence.target: when thou makest a feast, call the poor, feeble, lame, and blind

4:17.note: Bread eaten with the hungry and needy becomes, on Christ's lips, the feast to which the poor who cannot repay are called.

evidence.source: God be in your journey, and his Angel accompany you
evidence.target: will send his Angel with thee, & will direct thy way

5:21.note: Abraham sent his servant with an angel promised, to take a wife for his son from his own kindred; Tobias sends his son the same way, and the angel goes with him to a kinswoman's marriage.

evidence.source: she had been delivered to seven husbands
evidence.target: whose wife of the seven shall she be? For they all had her

3:8.note: The Sadducees' riddle — one woman, seven husbands — is Sara's history turned against the resurrection; in Tobias a devil, not levirate duty, left her seven times widowed.

evidence.source: with tears kissed him, and weeping upon his neck
evidence.target: he ran forth to meet him, & embracing him & heartily kissing him

7:7.note: As Laban ran forth to embrace and kiss Jacob his sister's son at his journey's end, so Raguel receives Tobias with tears, kissing him and weeping upon his neck.

evidence.source: Raphael the Angel took the devil, & bound him in the desert
evidence.target: which is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years

8:3.note: Raphael taking the devil Asmodeus and binding him in the desert is the first picture of John's angel apprehending the devil and Satan and binding him.

evidence.source: Thou madest Adam of the slime of the earth
evidence.target: Our Lord God therefore formed man of the slime of the earth

8:8.note: The wedding-night prayer retells the creation it blesses: Adam formed of the slime of the earth, and Eve given him for an helper.

evidence.source: alms delivereth from death, and that is it which purgeth sins
evidence.target: redeem thou thy sins with alms, & thine iniquities

12:9.note: Raphael's doctrine, that alms purgeth sins, is Daniel's counsel to the king: redeem thou thy sins with alms.

evidence.source: I offered thy prayer to our Lord
evidence.target: he should give of the prayers of all saints upon the altar of gold

12:12.note: Raphael offered Tobias's prayer to the Lord; in the Apocalypse the angel gives the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar before God's throne.

evidence.source: I am Raphael an Angel, one of the seven, which assist before our Lord
evidence.target: I saw seven Angels standing in the sight of God

12:15.note: Raphael names himself one of the seven that assist before the Lord; John sees those seven angels standing in the sight of God.

evidence.source: I am Raphael an Angel, one of the seven, which assist before our Lord
evidence.target: I am Gabriel that assist before God

12:15.note: Gabriel declares himself in Raphael's own form: I am —, that assist before God.

evidence.source: leadest down to hell, and bringest back again
evidence.target: bringeth down to hell and fetcheth back again

13:2.note: Tobias's song takes up Anna's sentence in her own words: God bringeth down to hell and fetcheth back again.

evidence.source: thou scourgest, and savest: leadest down to hell, and bringest back again
evidence.target: bringest down to the gates of death, and fetchest again

13:2.note: Tobias and Wisdom sing Anna's sentence together: God bringeth down to the gates of death, and fetcheth back again.

evidence.source: there is none that may escape thy hand
evidence.target: there is none that can deliver out of my hand

13:2.note: Moses' song ends the matter as Tobias does: there is none that can deliver out of God's hand.

evidence.source: Thou shalt shine with a glorious light
evidence.target: the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and kings in the brightness

13:13.note: Jerusalem shining with a glorious light in Tobias's song is Isaias's Jerusalem, in whose light the Gentiles walk and kings in the brightness of her rising.

evidence.source: Nations from far shall come to thee: and bringing gifts
evidence.target: the kings of the earth shall bring their glory and honour into it

13:14.note: The nations coming from far with gifts to adore the Lord in Jerusalem are the kings of the earth bringing their glory and honour into John's city.

evidence.source: they shall all be blessed, and shall be gathered together to our Lord
evidence.target: all these are gathered together, they are come to thee

13:17.note: Jerusalem's children gathered together to the Lord is Isaias's gathering: all these are gathered together, they are come to thee.

evidence.source: The gates of Jerusalem shall be built of Sapphire and the Emerald
evidence.target: the second, the sapphire: the third, the calcedonius: the fourth, the emerald

13:21.note: Tobias builds Jerusalem's gates of sapphire and emerald; the foundations of John's city are adorned with the same stones among the twelve.

evidence.source: The destruction of Ninive is near: for the word of our Lord faileth not
evidence.target: As yet forty days, and Ninive shall be subverted

14:6.note: Dying Tobias foretells the fall Jonas preached in Ninive's streets — the word once delayed by the city's repentance, not failed.

evidence.source: Then was the Kingdom of Nabuchodonosor exalted, and his heart was elevated
evidence.target: when his heart was elevated, and his spirit obstinately set to pride

1:7.note: Daniel says of Nabuchodonosor in nearly the same words what Judith's first chapter says: his heart was elevated, and for it he was deposed from his throne.

evidence.source: they laid the infants prostrate against the face of the temple
evidence.target: gather together the little ones, & them that suck the breasts

4:9.note: In Judith's solemn fast even the infants are laid prostrate before the temple, as Joel's fast gathers the little ones and them that suck the breasts.

evidence.source: and the altar of our Lord they covered with hair-cloth
evidence.target: the priests our Lord's ministers shall weep, & shall say

4:9.note: Judith's priests minister in hair-cloth with the altar itself covered in hair-cloth, as Joel's priests, the Lord's ministers, weep before the altar in the fast.

evidence.source: I may shew thee that there is no God but Nabuchodonosor
evidence.target: what God is there that shall deliver you out of my hand?

6:2.note: Holofernes' sentence, that there is no God but Nabuchodonosor, is the king's own challenge in Daniel: what God is there that shall deliver you out of my hand?

evidence.source: I may shew thee that there is no God but Nabuchodonosor
evidence.target: that the Lord can deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?

6:2.note: The Assyrian boast over Bethulia is Sennacherib's taunt over Jerusalem: which god ever delivered his country, that the Lord should deliver his city out of my hand?

evidence.source: We have sinned with our fathers, we have done unjustly
evidence.target: We have sinned with our fathers: we have dealt unjustly

7:19.note: The besieged people's confession takes up the psalm's words: we have sinned with our fathers, we have done unjustly, we have committed iniquity.

evidence.source: that they say not among the Gentiles: Where is their God?
evidence.target: Lest they say perhaps amongst the Gentiles: where is their God?

7:21.note: The people's dread, lest the Gentiles say 'Where is their God?', is the psalm's dread in nearly the same words.

evidence.source: that they say not among the Gentiles: Where is their God?
evidence.target: Why say they in the peoples: Where is their God?

7:21.note: Joel's priests plead against the same reproach Judith's people cry aloud: why say they among the peoples, Where is their God?

evidence.source: she fasted all the days of her life
evidence.target: by fastings and prayers serving night and day

8:6.note: Judith, the widow who fasted all the days of her life, stands behind Anna, the widow who departed not from the temple, by fastings and prayers serving night and day.

evidence.source: And what are you, that tempt our Lord?
evidence.target: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God

8:11.note: Judith's rebuke of the elders who set God a five-day term speaks the law of Massah: thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

evidence.source: And what are you, that tempt our Lord?
evidence.target: Why chide you against me? Wherefore do you tempt our Lord?

8:11.note: Her question to the ancients is Moses' rebuke at the waters of contradiction in the same form: wherefore do you tempt our Lord?

evidence.source: how our father Abraham was tempted, and by many tribulations proved
evidence.target: God tempted Abraham, and said to him: Abraham, Abraham

8:22.note: Judith bids the elders remember Abraham, whom God tempted and who through many tribulations was proved and made the friend of God.

evidence.source: were destroyed of the destroyer, and perished by serpents
evidence.target: our Lord sent upon the people fiery serpents

8:25.note: The fathers Judith warns the elders against perished by the fiery serpents the Lord sent upon the murmuring people in the desert.

evidence.source: were destroyed of the destroyer, and perished by serpents
evidence.target: as certain of them murmured, and perished by the destroyer

8:25.note: Judith's two strokes, destroyed of the destroyer and perished by serpents, are Paul's two warnings to the Corinthians drawn from the same desert story.

evidence.source: Lord God of my father Simeon, who gavest him a sword
evidence.target: Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina, taking their swords

9:2.note: Judith prays by the sword God gave her father Simeon, who with Levi took his sword into Sichem against the ravishers of their sister Dina.

evidence.source: But thou didst look over their camp, and darkness wearied them
evidence.target: behold our Lord looking upon the Ægyptians' camp through the pillar

9:7.note: She asks God to look on the Assyrians as he looked upon the Egyptians' camp through the pillar of fire and slew their army.

evidence.source: The depth held their feet, and the waters overwhelmed them
evidence.target: And the waters returned, and overwhelmed the chariots & the horsemen

9:8.note: Her prayer remembers the sea: the depth held their feet, as the returning waters overwhelmed Pharaoh's chariots and horsemen, and not one remained.

evidence.source: which trust in their multitude, and in their chariots
evidence.target: These in chariots, and these in horses: but we will invocate

9:9.note: Against the Assyrians who trust in their multitude and their chariots Judith prays the psalm's confession: these in chariots, but we will invocate the name of the Lord.

evidence.source: which destroyest wars from the beginning, and Lord is thy name
evidence.target: taking away wars even unto the end of the earth

9:10.note: The God who destroyest wars from the beginning is the psalm's God, taking away wars even unto the end of the earth.

evidence.source: For not in multitude is thy power o Lord
evidence.target: shall not be saved in the multitude of his strength

9:16.note: Her 'not in multitude is thy power, neither in strength of horses' is the psalm's: the giant shall not be saved in the multitude of his strength, and the horse faileth to safety.

evidence.source: but the prayer of the humble and meek hath always pleased thee
evidence.target: hath deposed the mighty from their seat, & hath exalted the humble

9:16.note: The God whom the proud never pleased from the beginning, but whose ear the humble and meek always had, is Mary's God, who deposes the mighty from their seat and exalts the humble.

evidence.source: acknowledge that thou art God, and there is no other besides thee
evidence.target: our Lord he is God, and there is none other besides him

9:19.note: Her prayer ends where Solomon's prayer at the dedication ended: that all nations may acknowledge thou art God, and there is no other besides thee.

evidence.source: and she struck twice upon his neck, and cut off his head
evidence.target: she put the nail upon the temple of his head

13:10.note: As Jael struck the sleeping Sisera through the head in her tent, Judith strikes the sleeping, drunken Holofernes twice upon the neck in his chamber and cuts off his head.

evidence.source: the Lord our God struck him by the hand of a woman
evidence.target: Sisara shall be delivered into the hand of a woman

13:19.note: Judith's own word over the severed head, that the Lord struck him by the hand of a woman, answers Deborah's word that Sisara should be delivered into the hand of a woman.

evidence.source: because he is good, because his mercy is for ever
evidence.target: because he is good: because his mercy is for ever

13:21.note: Her thanksgiving opens with the psalms' standing refrain (the same opening stands at Psalms 106:1, 117:1 and 135:1): confess ye to our Lord, because he is good, because his mercy is for ever.

evidence.source: Blessed art thou daughter of our Lord the high God, above all
evidence.target: Blessed among women be Jahel the wife of Haber the Cineite

13:23.note: Ozias blesses Judith above all women upon the earth, as Deborah's song blessed Jael among women for the same deed against the same kind of foe.

evidence.source: Blessed art thou daughter of our Lord the high God
evidence.target: Blessed art thou among women

13:23.note: The blessing spoken over the woman through whom God slew her people's enemy, blessed art thou, is Elizabeth's blessing over the woman who bore her people's Saviour.

evidence.source: Then sang Judith this song to our Lord, saying
evidence.target: Debbora and Barac the son of Abinoem sang in that day, saying

16:1.note: As Deborah sang in that day over Sisera fallen by a woman's hand, Judith sings her song to the Lord over Holofernes.

evidence.source: Begin ye to our Lord in timbrels, sing ye to our Lord
evidence.target: and all the women went forth after her with timbrels and dances

16:2.note: Her timbrels are Miriam's, who took a timbrel in her hand and led all the women forth with timbrels when Pharaoh's host fell.

evidence.source: Our Lord confoundeth battles, Lord is his name
evidence.target: Our Lord is a man of war, Omnipotent is his name

16:3.note: Her 'Lord is his name' over confounded battles answers the song at the sea: our Lord is a man of war, Omnipotent is his name.

evidence.source: hath delivered him into the hands of a woman
evidence.target: Sisara shall be delivered into the hand of a woman

16:7.note: Her canticle itself names the pattern: the Lord omnipotent delivered the mighty one into the hands of a woman, as Deborah foretold that Sisara would be delivered into the hand of a woman.

evidence.source: because thou saidst, and they were made
evidence.target: he said, and they were made: he commanded and they were created

16:17.note: Her creation line takes the psalm's up almost word for word: thou saidst, and they were made.

evidence.source: thou didst send thy spirit, and they were created
evidence.target: Thou shalt send forth thy spirit, and they shall be created

16:17.note: The second half of the same verse, thou didst send thy spirit and they were created, is the psalm's word on the Spirit sent forth to create and renew.

evidence.source: the rocks shall melt as wax before thy face
evidence.target: The mountains melted as wax, before the face of our Lord

16:18.note: Rocks melting as wax before his face is the psalm's mountains melted as wax before the face of our Lord.

evidence.source: For he will give fire, and worms into their flesh
evidence.target: their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched

16:21.note: Fire and worms given into the flesh, to burn and to be felt for ever, is Isaiah's sentence on the men that transgressed: their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched.

evidence.source: To the Lord our God justice: but to us confusion of our face
evidence.target: To thee o Lord, justice: but to us confusion of face

1:15.note: The confession opens with Daniel's own sentence: to the Lord justice, but to us confusion of face.

evidence.source: but to us confusion of our face: as is this day
evidence.target: into confusion of countenance, as also at this day

1:15.note: Esdras's confession ends where Baruch's begins: delivered into captivity, and into confusion of countenance, as also at this day.

evidence.source: many evils and maledictions have cloven to us
evidence.target: the malediction hath distilled upon us, & the detestation

1:20.note: Both prayers say the malediction written in the law of Moses the servant has come upon Israel and clings to them.

evidence.source: were not done under the heaven, as have been done in Jerusalem
evidence.target: a great evil, such as never was under all the heaven

2:2.note: Baruch measures Jerusalem's calamity with Daniel's measure: a great evil such as was never done under all the heaven.

evidence.source: eat the flesh of his son, and the flesh of his daughter
evidence.target: the flesh of thy sons & of thy daughters

2:3.note: The siege-curse of Deuteronomy, that a man should eat the flesh of his son and daughter, is the very evil Baruch sees come upon Jerusalem.

evidence.source: we have not besought the face of the Lord our God
evidence.target: we besought not thy face o Lord our God

2:8.note: Both confessions admit the same omission in the same words: we besought not the face of the Lord our God.

evidence.source: our Lord is just in all his works
evidence.target: just is the Lord our God in all his works

2:9.note: Both confessions acquit God in one breath: the Lord is just in all his works, and we have not heard his voice.

evidence.source: and madest thee a name as is this day
evidence.target: madest thee a name according to this day

2:11.note: Both prayers name God by the exodus: he brought his people out of Egypt in a strong hand, and made himself a name as it is this day.

evidence.source: we have sinned, we have done impiously, we have dealt unjustly
evidence.target: We have sinned with our fathers: we have dealt unjustly

2:12.note: Baruch's triple confession, we have sinned and dealt unjustly, is the psalm's own confession for Israel and her fathers.

evidence.source: Let thy wrath be turned away from us
evidence.target: but let thy wrath be turned away I beseech thee

2:13.note: The plea is Daniel's plea in Daniel's words: let thy wrath be turned away from us.

evidence.source: incline thine ear, and hear us
evidence.target: Incline my God thine ear, & hear

2:16.note: Baruch prays Daniel's prayer for the desolate sanctuary: incline thine ear, and hear.

evidence.source: shall not give honour and justification to our Lord
evidence.target: Because hell shall not confess to thee, neither shall death praise thee

2:17.note: Baruch argues as Ezechias argued: the dead in hell shall not confess thee, so hear the living soul that sorrows.

evidence.source: do works for the king of Babylon
evidence.target: submit their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon

2:21.note: The word Baruch quotes over the exiles is Jeremias's yoke-oracle: submit the neck and serve the king of Babylon, and remain in the land.

evidence.source: the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride
evidence.target: the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride

2:23.note: Baruch takes up Jeremias's sentence whole: God takes away the voice of joy, of the bridegroom, and of the bride.

evidence.source: and pray ye for the life of Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon
evidence.target: seek the peace of the city, to which I have transported you

1:11.note: Baruch's letter enacts Jeremias's own command to the captives: seek the peace of Babylon, and pray for the king under whose shadow they live.

evidence.source: and I will give them a heart, and they shall understand
evidence.target: I will give them an heart to know me

2:31.note: The heart God promises the returning exiles in Jeremias, a heart to know him, is the heart Baruch says he will give, with ears that hear.

evidence.source: I will recall them back into the land
evidence.target: will bring thee again from thy captivity, and have mercy upon thee

2:34.note: Moses promised that God would bring Israel back from captivity and gather them again; Baruch hears that promise spoken over his own dispersion.

evidence.source: And I will establish unto them another testament everlasting
evidence.target: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them

2:35.note: Baruch's 'another testament everlasting' restates the everlasting covenant of Jeremias 32, that God be their God and they his people.

evidence.source: Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom
evidence.target: Me they have forsaken the fountain of living water

3:12.note: Jeremias's forsaken fountain of living water becomes in Baruch the forsaken fountain of wisdom: the leaving is the same leaving.

evidence.source: Who hath found the place thereof? and who hath entered into the treasures thereof?
evidence.target: But where is wisdom to be found, and what is the place of understanding?

3:15.note: Baruch's hymn opens with Job's unanswered question: where is wisdom to be found, and who has found her place?

evidence.source: Who hath ascended into heaven, and taken her
evidence.target: that thou mayest say: Which of us is able to ascend unto heaven

3:29.note: Baruch asks of wisdom herself the question Moses asked of the commandment: who shall ascend into heaven to bring her to us?

evidence.source: Who hath passed over the sea, and found her
evidence.target: that thou mayest pretend, and say: Which of us can pass over the sea

3:30.note: And Moses' second question follows: who can pass over the sea to bring her to us?

evidence.source: he that knoweth all things, knoweth her
evidence.target: God understandeth the way of it, & he knoweth the place thereof

3:32.note: Job's answer stands in Baruch too: no man knows wisdom's way, but he that knoweth all things knoweth her.

evidence.source: After these things he was seen upon the earth, and was conversant with men
evidence.target: And The Word Was Made Flesh, and dwelt in us

3:38.note: Baruch's word that God was seen upon the earth and conversed with men is the sentence the Church has always heard again in John's prologue.

evidence.source: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law
evidence.target: For this is your wisdom, and understanding before peoples

4:1.note: Deuteronomy said the commandments kept would be Israel's wisdom and understanding before the peoples; Baruch names that wisdom: the book of the commandments itself.

evidence.source: Because thou sittest for ever, and shall we perish everlastingly?
evidence.target: But thou o Lord shalt remain for ever

3:3.note: The prayer of chapter 3 opens where Lamentations ends: thou, Lord, remainest for ever — shall we perish everlastingly?

evidence.source: rejoice over me a widow, and desolate: I am forsaken of many
evidence.target: how is the lady of the Gentiles become as a widow

4:12.note: Jerusalem speaks in Baruch with Lamentations' own figure: the lady of the Gentiles become as a widow, and forsaken.

evidence.source: I have seen the captivity of my people, and of my sons, and daughters
evidence.target: my children are become desolate because the enemy hath prevailed

4:10.note: The mother of Lamentations weeps because her children are become desolate; Baruch's Jerusalem has seen the captivity of her sons and daughters.

evidence.source: Be of good comfort Jerusalem: for he exhorteth thee, that named thee
evidence.target: Be comforted, be comforted my people, saith your God

4:30.note: The whole consolation of Baruch 4 and 5 takes up the word that opens Isaias's book of comfort: be comforted, my people.

evidence.source: whom thou hast let go dispersed, they come gathered together
evidence.target: Our Lord building up Jerusalem: will gather together the dispersions of Israel

4:37.note: The psalm's promise that the Lord building Jerusalem will gather together the dispersions of Israel is Baruch's closing sight: the dispersed come gathered together.

evidence.source: and put on the beauty, and honor of that everlasting glory
evidence.target: put on the garments of thy glory o Jerusalem

5:1.note: Isaias bade Jerusalem put on the garments of her glory; Baruch tells her to put off the robe of mourning and put that everlasting glory on.

evidence.source: God will clothe thee with the doublet of justice
evidence.target: and with the garment of justice he hath compassed me

5:2.note: The doublet of justice God clothes Jerusalem with in Baruch is Isaias's garment of justice, worn with the garments of salvation.

evidence.source: Arise Jerusalem, and stand on high: and look about toward the East
evidence.target: Arise, be illuminated Jerusalem: because thy light is come

5:5.note: Baruch's 'Arise, Jerusalem' takes up Isaias's call to the city whose light is come.

evidence.source: see thy children gathered together from the rising of the sun
evidence.target: all these are gathered together, they are come to thee

5:5.note: What Jerusalem is told to look and see is Isaias's sight: her children gathered together, come to her from afar.

evidence.source: to humble every high mountain, and everlasting rocks, and to fill up valleys
evidence.target: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and little hill shall be humbled

5:7.note: God's road home for Israel in Baruch is Isaias's road: every valley filled up, and every high mountain humbled.

evidence.source: so shall she be made sorrowful in her own desolation
evidence.target: I shall not sit a widow, and I shall not know barrenness

4:33.note: Babylon swore she would never sit a widow nor know loss; Baruch answers that the city which rejoiced in Jerusalem's ruin shall be made sorrowful in her own desolation.

evidence.source: and she shall be inhabited of devils a great time
evidence.target: and it is become the habitation of devils

4:35.note: Baruch's sentence on the city that held her children — fire from the Everlasting, and inhabited of devils for a long time — is Babylon's sentence in the Apocalypse.

evidence.source: to be carried upon shoulders, shewing fear to the Gentiles
evidence.target: They bear him on their shoulders carrying, and setting him in his place

6:3.note: The first sight of the epistle, gods of gold and wood carried upon shoulders, is Isaias's carried god, set in his place and unable to move from it.

evidence.source: are false things, and they cannot speak
evidence.target: They have mouth, and shall not speak: they have eyes, an shall not see

6:7.note: The epistle's idols that cannot speak are the psalm's idols: they have mouth, and shall not speak; eyes, and shall not see.

evidence.source: Whereby you may know that they are not gods. Therefore fear them not
evidence.target: Therefore fear them not, because they can neither do ill nor well

6:22.note: The epistle's refrain is Jeremias's own: fear them not, for they are not gods, and can neither do ill nor well.

evidence.source: With all price are they bought, whereas there is no breath in them
evidence.target: it is false that he hath melted, and there is no spirit in them

6:24.note: Jeremias's craftsman is confounded in a sculptile with no spirit in it; the epistle's gods, bought at full price, have no breath in them.

evidence.source: but the works of men's hands, and no work of God is with them
evidence.target: The idols of the Gentiles are silver, and gold, the works of men's hands

6:50.note: The epistle's verdict is the psalm's first line on idols: silver and gold, the works of men's hands — and no work of God in them.

evidence.source: who when they hear that the dumb cannot speak, they offer it to Bel
evidence.target: this same is within of clay, and without of brass

6:40.note: The epistle names Bel himself, whose worshippers beg a dumb god to speak; Daniel's Bel is that same god, clay within and brass without, that never ate at any time.

evidence.source: For as in a garden of cucumbers a scarecrow keepeth nothing
evidence.target: They are framed after the similitude of a palm tree, & shall not speak

6:69.note: Jeremias's idol stands like a post that cannot speak; the epistle gives the same figure its other form, a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers that keepeth nothing.

evidence.source: and should prohibit holocausts & sacrifices
evidence.target: the continual sacrifice shall be taken away

1:47.note: Antiochus's prohibition of holocausts and sacrifices in the temple is Daniel's taking away of the continual sacrifice, before the abomination is set up.

evidence.source: built the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God
evidence.target: they shall give abomination into desolation

1:57.note: The arms of Daniel's prophecy pollute the sanctuary of strength and set up the abomination; Antiochus builds it upon the altar of God.

evidence.source: the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God
evidence.target: the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet

1:57.note: Our Lord warns of the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel, standing in the holy place; its first historical standing is this idol upon the altar.

evidence.source: remember the works of the fathers, which they have done in their generations
evidence.target: Let us praise glorious men, and our fathers in their generation

2:51.note: Mathathias's dying testament opens the same roll of the fathers in their generation that Sirach opened, that the sons may receive great glory and an eternal name.

evidence.source: and it was reputed to him unto justice
evidence.target: Abram believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice

2:52.note: Mathathias tells Abraham's faithfulness in Genesis 15's own clause: it was reputed to him unto justice.

evidence.source: Abraham was he not in tentation found faithful
evidence.target: By faith, Abraham offered Isaac, when he was tempted

2:52.note: Hebrews sings the same temptation: Abraham offered Isaac when he was tempted, and was found faithful.

evidence.source: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment
evidence.target: can I do this wicked thing, and sin against my God?

2:53.note: The seed carries Joseph's lordship from Genesis 41; his keeping of the commandment in distress is Potiphar's house, where he will not sin against his God.

evidence.source: received the testament of an everlasting Priesthood
evidence.target: reputed to him unto justice, in generation and generation even for ever

2:54.note: The psalm reckons Phinees's zeal with Abraham's formula, reputed unto justice for ever, where Numbers 25, carried by the seed, gives the priesthood covenant itself.

evidence.source: Jesus whilst he accomplished the word, was made the Duke in Israel
evidence.target: Josue therefore took all the Land, as our Lord spake to Moyses

2:55.note: Jesus the son of Nun accomplished the word when he took all the land, as the Lord had spoken to Moyses, and delivered it in possession to Israel.

evidence.source: Caleb whilst he testifieth in the Church, received an inheritance
evidence.target: And Josue blessed him, and delivered to him Hebron in possession

2:56.note: The seed carries Caleb's testimony among the spies from Numbers 14; the inheritance he received is Hebron, delivered to him in possession.

evidence.source: David in his mercy obtained the seat of the kingdom for ever
evidence.target: and thy Kingdom for ever before thy face

2:57.note: David's everlasting seat is Nathan's promise: thy kingdom for ever before thy face, and thy throne firm continually.

evidence.source: Elias whilst he zealeth the zeal of the law
evidence.target: With zeal have I been zealous for our Lord the God of hosts

2:58.note: The seed carries Elias's receiving into heaven from 4 Kings 2; his zeal is his own word on Horeb, with zeal have I been zealous for the Lord.

evidence.source: believing, were delivered out of the flame
evidence.target: extinguished the force of fire

2:59.note: Hebrews gathers the three children's deliverance into one clause: by faith they extinguished the force of fire.

evidence.source: Daniel in his simplicity was delivered out of the lions' mouth
evidence.target: hath sent his Angel, and hath shut up the mouths of the lions

2:60.note: The seed's margin cites Daniel 5, but the lions' mouths shut by God's angel stand in Daniel 6, where Daniel tells the king of his deliverance.

evidence.source: was delivered out of the lions' mouth
evidence.target: stopped the mouths of lions

2:60.note: Hebrews's roll of faith keeps Daniel's image: by faith they stopped the mouths of lions.

evidence.source: he is turned into his earth, & his cogitation is perished
evidence.target: return into his earth: in that day all their cogitations shall perish

2:63.note: Mathathias's warning against the sinful man's glory takes up the psalm's sentence on princes: turned into his earth, and his cogitation perished.

evidence.source: Remember in what sort our fathers were saved in the red sea
evidence.target: delivered Israel in that day out of the hand of the Ægyptians

4:9.note: Judas heartens his men with the fathers' first deliverance: saved in the Red Sea when Pharao with a great army followed them.

evidence.source: fire came down from heaven, and consumed the holocaust
evidence.target: fire descended from heaven, and devoured the holocausts & victims

2:10.note: The verse names Moyses and Salomon in one breath; the seed carries the Moyses half from the next verse to Leviticus 9:24, and Salomon's fire, falling when his prayer ended, stands here.

evidence.source: which die for his laws, in the resurrection of eternal life
evidence.target: shall awake: some unto life everlasting

7:9.note: The second brother's hope, to be raised by the King of the world in the resurrection of eternal life, is Daniel's awakening of the sleepers: some unto life everlasting.

evidence.source: will raise us up which die for his laws
evidence.target: were racked, not accepting redemption, that they might find a better resurrection

7:9.note: Hebrews's racked ones, not accepting redemption that they might find a better resurrection, are these brethren on the wheel and in the frying pan.

evidence.source: For to thee there shall not be resurrection unto life
evidence.target: others unto reproach to see it always

7:14.note: The fourth brother denies Antiochus the other half of Daniel's awakening: for thee there shall not be resurrection unto life, but reproach to see it always.

evidence.source: that in that mercy I may receive thee again with thy brethren
evidence.target: women received of resurrection their dead

7:29.note: The mother who hopes to receive her son again in that mercy stands at the head of Hebrews's women who received of resurrection their dead.

evidence.source: that in that mercy I may receive thee again with thy brethren
evidence.target: and took her son, and went out

7:29.note: The Sunamitess took up her son alive in this life; the Machabee mother expects to receive hers again in the resurrection mercy, and Hebrews 11:35 holds the two mothers in one verse.

evidence.source: I obey not the commandment of the king
evidence.target: God must be obeyed, rather than men

7:30.note: The youngest brother's refusal, the king's commandment set against the law given by Moyses, is Peter's rule before the council: God must be obeyed, rather than men.

evidence.source: struck him with an uncurable and invisible plague
evidence.target: our Lord struck him with an incurable disease of the belly

9:5.note: Antiochus, struck with a cruel plague of the bowels he had tormented in others, dies Joram's death: the Lord struck him with an incurable disease of the belly.

evidence.source: now being humbled to the ground
evidence.target: them that walk in pride he can humble

9:8.note: He that was replenished with pride above the measure of man, and would weigh the mountains in a balance, now humbled to the ground in a litter, learns Nabuchodonosor's confession: them that walk in pride he can humble.

evidence.source: out of the body of the impious man, worms crawled abundantly
evidence.target: being consumed of worms, he gave up the ghost

9:9.note: Herod, struck by the angel because he had not given the honour to God, and consumed of worms, dies Antiochus's death before the Church's eyes.

evidence.source: all the nation of the Jews every year to keep these days
evidence.target: And the Dedication was in Jerusalem: and it was winter

10:8.note: The days decreed here, to be kept every year by all the nation of the Jews, are the Dedication John finds celebrated in Jerusalem in winter, when Jesus walked in Salomon's porch.

evidence.source: unless he hoped that they that were slain should rise again
evidence.target: baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not again at all

12:44.note: Judas's sacrifice for the dead and Paul's baptism for the dead rest on one argument: the practice is superfluous and vain unless the dead rise again.

evidence.source: had taken their sleep with godliness, had very good grace laid up
evidence.target: many of those, that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake

12:45.note: The slain who took their sleep with godliness, with very good grace laid up for them, are Daniel's sleepers in the dust of the earth who shall awake.

evidence.source: this is he that prayeth much for the people
evidence.target: If Moyses & Samuel shall stand before me

15:14.note: Onias names Jeremias the prophet who prayeth much for the people and for the whole city; Jeremias's own book sets the measure of such intercession, Moyses and Samuel standing before God.

evidence.source: understand that God of nothing made them & mankind
evidence.target: In the beginning GOD created heaven and earth

7:28.note: The mother of the seven brethren states Genesis 1 as a doctrine of faith: heaven, earth, and all in them, and mankind also, God made of nothing.

evidence.source: two great dragons, prepared one against another into battle
evidence.target: But the two dragons: I am, and Aman

11:6.note: The dream's two dragons are named by the interpretation the book itself prints: Mardochaeus and Aman.

evidence.source: a little fountain grew into a very great river

evidence.source: Fire and heat bless ye our Lord

evidence.source: Ice and snows bless ye our Lord
evidence.target: Fire, hail, snow, ice, spirit of storms

evidence.source: Mountains and little hills bless ye our Lord
evidence.target: Mountains, and all little hills

evidence.source: Whales, and all things that move in the waters

evidence.source: All beasts and cattle bless ye our Lord

evidence.source: Let Israel bless our Lord
evidence.target: to the children of Israel a people approaching unto him

evidence.source: Spirits and souls of the just bless ye our Lord
evidence.target: An hymn to all his saints

evidence.source: Eternal God, which art the knower of hidden things

evidence.source: thou knowest that they have borne false witness against me

evidence.source: they did to them as they had dealt naughtily against their neighbour

evidence.source: I worship not idols made with hand

evidence.source: I worship not idols made with hand

evidence.source: I worship not idols made with hand
evidence.target: who have called the works of men's hands gods

evidence.source: he delivered Bel into the power of Daniel: who overthrew him
evidence.target: Bel is broken, Nabo is destroyed

evidence.source: Who cast him into the lake of lions
evidence.target: they brought Daniel, and cast him into the lake of lions

evidence.source: he drew him out of the lake of lions
evidence.target: Daniel was brought out of the lake

evidence.source: he cast into the lake, and they were devoured in a moment

evidence.target: God that commanded light to shine of darkness

evidence.source: a greater light to govern the day

evidence.source: God created man to his own image
evidence.target: he is the image and glory of God

evidence.target: there is a God in heaven that revealeth mysteries

40:8.note: Joseph and Daniel, the two dream-readers set before kings, make the same disclaimer: interpretation belongs to God, who revealeth mysteries.

evidence.source: these are the names of the children of Israel, that entered into Ægypt, himself with his children
evidence.target: These be the names of the children of Israel, that entered into Ægypt with Jacob

46:8.note: Exodus opens by taking up Genesis' list-formula to the letter: these are the names of the children of Israel that entered into Egypt.

evidence.source: All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Ægypt, were seventy
evidence.target: all the souls that came out of Jacob's thigh were seventy

46:27.note: Exodus repeats Genesis' reckoning of the descent: seventy souls of the house of Jacob.

evidence.source: The days of the pilgrimage of my life are an hundred thirty years, few and evil
evidence.target: we are pilgrims before thee, and strangers, as all our fathers

47:9.note: David's prayer takes Jacob's own word for his years — pilgrimage — and makes it the confession of all the fathers.

evidence.source: was increased, & multiplied exceedingly
evidence.target: the children of Israel increased, and as it were springing up did multiply, and growing strong exceedingly, filled the land

47:27.note: Exodus' first paragraph resumes Genesis' last word on the sojourn: Israel increased and multiplied exceedingly, even under a new king that knew not Joseph.

evidence.source: his younger brother shall be greater than he: and his seed shall grow into nations
evidence.target: These are the multitudes of Ephraim, and these the thousands of Manasses

48:19.note: Moses' blessing of Joseph reckons what Jacob foresaw with crossed hands: Ephraim the younger grown into multitudes.

evidence.source: thou didst ascend thy father's bed, and didst defile his couch
evidence.target: when he had violated his father's bed, his first-birth-right was given to the sons of Joseph

49:4.note: The Chronicler explains Ruben's lost birthright out of Jacob's dying sentence: he had violated his father's bed.

evidence.source: taking thy rest thou didst lie as a lion, and as it were a lioness, who shall raise him up?
evidence.target: Lying he hath slept as a lion, and as a lioness, whom none shall be bold to raise up

49:9.note: Balaam's oracle on Israel couches in Jacob's own lion-words over Juda, taking his rest none dares rouse.

evidence.source: Till he do Come That is to be Sent
evidence.target: A star Shall Rise out of Jacob, and a rod shall arise from Israel

49:10.note: Balaam's star out of Jacob and rod out of Israel answer Jacob's sceptre that shall not be taken from Juda till he come that is to be sent.

evidence.source: The Sceptre Shall Not be Taken Away From Judas
evidence.target: till he came to whom judgement belongeth, and I will deliver it to him

49:10.note: Ezechiel's triple 'iniquity, iniquity, iniquity' over the diadem runs till he come to whom judgment belongeth — the term Jacob's sceptre-oracle set.

evidence.source: Dan shall judge his own people, as also another tribe in Israel
evidence.target: he judged Israel twenty years

49:16.note: Jacob's word on Dan is fulfilled in the one judge of Dan's stock: Samson, of Saraa, son of Manue (Judges 13:2), who judged Israel twenty years.

evidence.source: be they upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren
evidence.target: come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren

49:26.note: Moses' blessing of Joseph closes in Jacob's very words: the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, the Nazarite among his brethren.

evidence.source: You thought evil against me, but God turned that into good
evidence.target: to them that love God, all things cooperate unto good

50:20.note: Joseph's sentence is the doctrine in narrative form: evil thought against God's servant is turned by God into good, to save many peoples; Paul states it as the standing rule for them that love God.

evidence.source: God will visit you carry my bones with you out of this place
evidence.target: Moyses also took Joseph's bones with him: because he had adjured the children of Israel, saying: God shall visit you, carry out my bones from hence with you

50:24.note: Exodus records the oath kept at the going out: Moses took Joseph's bones, adjured in the words of Genesis 50.

evidence.source: God will visit you carry my bones with you out of this place
evidence.target: The bones also of Joseph which the children of Israel had taken out of Ægypt, they buried in Sichem

50:24.note: The bones carried out of Egypt under Joseph's adjuration are buried at last in Sichem, in the field Jacob bought — the oath's long journey ended where the patriarchs lie.

evidence.source: but the woman of the man
evidence.target: our Lord God built the rib which he took of Adam into a woman

11:8.note: Paul's 'woman of the man' states in a phrase what Genesis tells at length: the woman built from the rib taken out of Adam.

evidence.source: The first man of earth, earthly: the second man from Heaven, heavenly
evidence.target: formed man of the slime of the earth

15:47.note: The first man is 'of earth, earthly' because God formed him of the slime of the earth; the second man is set against him as from heaven.

evidence.source: as in Adam all die
evidence.target: dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return

15:22.note: The death that is in Adam for all men is the sentence of Genesis 3 itself: dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.

evidence.source: we curse men which are made after the similitude of God
evidence.target: Let us make Man to our image & likeness

3:9.note: James forbids cursing men on Genesis' ground: they are made after the similitude of God.

evidence.source: God made man right, and he hath entangled himself with infinite questions
evidence.target: God created man to his own image

7:30.note: The Preacher sums up the fall in one line: God made man right — created to his image — and man has entangled himself.

evidence.source: put on the new man which according to God is created in justice, and holiness of the truth
evidence.target: to the image of God he created him

4:24.note: The new man is created according to God, as man was first created to God's image: a creation renewed.

evidence.source: Hath not one God created us?
evidence.target: male and female he created them

2:10.note: Malachias argues brotherhood from the one creation: one God created them all, male and female — one human family under one Father, which is why despising a brother violates the covenant.

evidence.source: Was not Esau brother to Jacob, saith our Lord, and I loved Jacob
evidence.target: one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger

1:2.note: Malachias' 'I loved Jacob' is God's later word upon the oracle spoken before the twins were born: the elder shall serve the younger.

evidence.source: She is a tree of life to them that shall apprehend her
evidence.target: the tree of life also in the middle of Paradise

3:18.note: Wisdom is praised in Eden's own title: a tree of life to them that lay hold on her.

evidence.source: When he prepared the heavens, I was present
evidence.target: In the beginning GOD created heaven and earth

8:27.note: Wisdom speaks as present when the heavens were prepared: Genesis' creation contemplated from within, by her who was with the Maker before the earth was made.

evidence.source: I saw a new heaven and a new earth. For the first heaven, and the first earth was gone
evidence.target: In the beginning GOD created heaven and earth

21:1.note: The last book answers the first in its own words: the heaven and earth created in the beginning give place to a new heaven and a new earth.

evidence.source: no curse shall be any more
evidence.target: cursed is the earth in thy work: with much toiling shalt thou eat thereof

22:3.note: The end answers the beginning: in the city of God no curse shall be any more, where Eden heard the earth cursed in man's work.

evidence.source: that great dragon was cast forth, the old serpent, which is called the devil and Satan
evidence.target: the serpent also was more subtile than all the beasts of the earth

12:9.note: The Apocalypse names Eden's serpent outright: the old serpent, the devil and Satan, the seducer of the whole world.

evidence.source: death shall be no more, nor mourning, nor crying
evidence.target: in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death

21:4.note: The death threatened at the tree, and entered by the eating of it, is abolished in the new creation: death shall be no more — the last word of the story answering the sentence of its first sin.

evidence.source: I beheld the earth, and lo it was void, and a thing of nothing: and the heavens, & there was no light in them
evidence.target: the earth was void and vacant, and darkness was upon the face of the depth

4:23.note: Jeremias sees judgment as un-creation: the earth void again as before the first day, and the heavens without the light God made.

evidence.source: the mourning, and weeping of Rachel weeping for her children
evidence.target: Rachel therefore died, and was buried in the high way that leadeth to Ephrata

31:15.note: Rachel weeps in Jeremias from the grave Genesis records for her, on the high way that leadeth to Ephrata — the Bethlehem road.

evidence.source: the Heavens were before, and the earth, out of water, and through water, consisting by the word of God
evidence.target: the Spirit of God moved over the waters

3:5.note: Peter's scoffers wilfully forget the first world as Genesis shews it: earth consisting out of water and through water, by the word of God.

evidence.source: that world then, being overflowed with water perished
evidence.target: all flesh was consumed that moved upon the earth

3:6.note: The world that then perished, overflowed with water, is the flood of Genesis, when all flesh that moved upon the earth was consumed.

evidence.source: gathering the fowls of the heaven, and fishes of the sea
evidence.target: rule over the fishes and the sea, and fowls of the air

1:3.note: Sophonias' gathering-away of man, beast, fowl, and fish unmakes the order of Genesis 1 in reverse: judgment as de-creation.

evidence.source: we clay: and thou art our maker, and all we the works of thy hands
evidence.target: formed man of the slime of the earth

64:8.note: Isaiah's prayer takes its plea from the making of Adam: we are the clay, and the God who formed man of the slime of the earth is our maker and father.

evidence.source: he is a liar, & the father thereof
evidence.target: the serpent said to the woman: No, you shall not die the death

8:44.note: The devil is a liar and the father of lies; his first recorded lie is the flat denial of God's word in Eden: No, you shall not die the death.

evidence.source: God sent his Son made of a woman, made under the Law
evidence.target: I will put enmity between thee & the woman, & thy seed and the seed of her

4:4.note: The promise in Eden ran between the serpent and the woman, her seed against his: in the fullness of time God sent his Son made of a woman, the woman's seed come to end the enmity.

evidence.source: on the Gentiles the blessing of Abraham might be made in Christ Jesus
evidence.target: IN Thee shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed

3:14.note: Paul names the blessing of Abraham made upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus: the kindreds of the earth blessed in Abraham, as was promised.

evidence.source: which is Agar
evidence.target: having an handmaid, an Ægyptian named Agar

4:24.note: Paul's allegory takes its figure from Genesis' plain introduction: Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, named Agar.

evidence.source: we brethren, according to Isaac, are the children of promise
evidence.target: she conceived & bare a son in her old age, at the time that God had foretold her

4:28.note: To be children of promise 'according to Isaac' is to be born as Isaac was: by promise, at the time God foretold, to parents in their old age.

evidence.source: all that take the sword shall perish with the sword
evidence.target: Whosoever shall shed man's blood, his blood shall be shed: for to the image of God man was made

26:52.note: The Lord's word in Gethsemane restates the flood covenant's law: blood for blood, and its reason — man made to the image of God.

evidence.source: Judas begat Phares and Zaram of Thamar
evidence.target: the other came forth: and the woman said: Why is the partition divided for thee? And for this cause called his name Phares

1:3.note: Matthew's genealogy keeps Thamar and her twins in the royal line: Phares, named for the partition divided at his birth.

evidence.source: he made of one, all mankind, to inhabit upon the whole face of the earth
evidence.target: of these was all mankind spread over the whole earth

17:26.note: Paul at Athens teaches Genesis 9: of Noe's three sons was all mankind spread over the whole earth.

evidence.source: every man heard them speak in his own tongue
evidence.target: let us go down, and there confound their tongue, that none may hear his neighbour's voice

2:6.note: Pentecost is Babel answered: there the tongue was confounded so that none might hear his neighbour's voice; here every man hears the great works of God in his own tongue.

evidence.source: called thither Jacob his father and all his kindred in seventy five souls
evidence.target: All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Ægypt, were seventy

7:14.note: Stephen reckons the kindred at seventy-five souls, following the Greek reckoning; Genesis as here printed numbers the house that entered Egypt at seventy.

evidence.source: it shall be more tolerable for Sodom in that day, than for that city
evidence.target: rained upon Sodome and Gomorre brimstone & fire from our Lord out of heaven

10:12.note: The Lord makes Sodom — the city rained on with fire — the measure of tolerableness in the day of judgment.

evidence.source: to whom thou swarest by thine own self, saying: I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven
evidence.target: I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is by the sea shore

32:13.note: Moses intercedes by pleading the sworn promise back to God: the stars of heaven, in the oath's own words.

evidence.source: Our Lord make this woman, which entereth into thy house, as Rachel, and Lia, which builded the house of Israel
evidence.target: opened her womb, her sister remaining barren

4:11.note: Bethlehem's elders bless Ruth in the names of Rachel and Lia, the two mothers who builded the house of Israel out of barren and opened wombs.

evidence.source: thy house may be, as the house of Phares, whom Thamar bare to Judas
evidence.target: for this cause called his name Phares

4:12.note: The blessing on Booz's house names its own ancestor: Phares, whom Thamar bare to Judas, named for the breach at his birth.
